chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Abu al-Qasim, from Hanan, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the found object (al-luqatah), and I was listening. He said: 'Announce it for a year. If you find its owner, then [return it]; otherwise, you are more entitled to it.' He said: 'It is like your own wealth.' He said: 'Choose for him, when he comes to you after a year, between its reward (compensation for keeping it) and paying it to him, if you had consumed it.'

key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found property or object picked up from the ground
key_terms.سَبِيلِ مَالِكَ: Like your own wealth (in terms of usage rights)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found property (Luqatah) and the rights of the finder and owner?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudence of *al-luqatah* (found property), establishing a one-year announcement period to locate the owner. The ruling distinguishes between the finder's right to keep the item if unclaimed and the liability for consumption, offering the owner a choice between compensation for the finder's effort or reimbursement for the consumed value. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the finder's diligence with the owner's property rights, ensuring fairness in transactional ethics.
